blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Habitat loss is the single largest cause of biodiversity decline, driven by agricultural and urban expansion.
Habitat fragmentation leads to species isolation and a significant reduction in gene flow.
Overexploitation stems from unsustainable biological harvesting, including excessive hunting, logging, and fishing.
Invasive alien species threaten ecosystem balance by outcompeting native flora and fauna.
Pollution directly disrupts critical food chains and organism reproductive systems.
Climate change forces habitats to shift faster than most species can naturally adapt.

blocks.content: Habitat Loss – largest cause; forests converted into agriculture and urban areas.
• Habitat Fragmentation – isolates species and reduces gene flow.
• Invasive Species – alien species outcompete natives.

items: Habitat loss is repeatedly tested as the #1 primary cause of global biodiversity loss.
Remember that Habitat Fragmentation specifically impacts genetic diversity by reducing gene flow.
Invasive species impact ecosystems primarily through competitive exclusion of native species.
